newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco to sell $300 mln in debt.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco to sell $300 mln in debt.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp plans to sell $300 million in debt on Thursday, according to market sources.
The sources said Merrrill Lynch & Co will be the lead manager of the offering, which is currently expected to consist of $200 million in 10-year debt and $100 million in seven-year debt.
Price talk on the 10-year debt calls for a spread of 215 basis points to 225 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
The seven-year tranche has price talk of 195 basis points to 200 basis points over comparable Treasuries.

A RJR Nabisco spokesman later confirmed the deal's size and structure. He noted that a shelf registration has already been filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission covering the amount to be issued. He was unable to confirm details about price talk.
He said the proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes including paying off commerical paper.

Asked why the company chose to bring the deal in the midst of intense market scrutiny of the tobacco industry's settlement talks, he said, "The market looks pretty good and like any good company with a sense of market conditions we are obviously taking advantage of it."

Lisa Gaffney, tobacco debt analyst at Bear Stearns & Co Inc noted, "If you think about it, the market for (tobacco companies) has been volatile for an extended period of time, and will show no signs of changing soon."
She added, "Given the favorable interest rate environment currently, it makes sense for them to tap this market."
Market sources said while the bonds will be rated Baa3/BBB-minus, price talk on the deal is more appropriate of bonds with double-B ratings.
Standard & Poor's has bonds of RJR and other major tobacco companies on CreditWatch with negative implications.
Gaffney said it should come as no surprise if the issue were to be priced at that level, given that prices of RJR debt in the secondary market currently reflect a double-B rating.
She noted spreads on RJR debt have actually tightened marginally on some positive news that followed the settlement announcement.
The company revealed in an 8-K filing with the SEC on Tuesday that it would only be responsible for $600 million of the $10 billion upfront payment in the settlement.
Market players had expected the company to be on the hook for $2.5 billion of the upfront settlement, based on its market shore.
